- When sentiment is high (≥0.65) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.30) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 2–3 periods.
- Model consistently underestimates the 10–15 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for longer horizons.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 0.5–2% upward bias if sentiment shifts to positive.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early periods (e.g., first 3–5 days of forecast); apply sentiment smoothing or lagged sentiment weighting for early horizon correction.
